newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, led by gold, silver.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, led by gold, silver.

text.p: Gold prices ended at a new four-and-a-quarter year low Monday, dragging silver prices lower also, but platinum group metals ended mixed, as another deadline for the resumption of Russian exports passed without any sign of metal deliveries, traders said.

"Gold is being led lower by more fund selling, and some further Australian producer hedging overnight, while silver broke down out of a two month old range setting off some stop-loss orders," Refco New York economist James Steel said.
COMEX August gold ended down 60 cents at $335.30 an ounce, after sliding to a fresh life-of-contract low at $334.60. Estimated total COMEX gold volume was 41,000 lots.

The latest slide has again been led by commodity fund selling, while investors have been driven away from precious metals investments by a strong U.S. stockmarket, a strong U.S. dollar and U.S. CPI inflation falling to a 10 year low.
Open interest in COMEX gold jumped 10,651 lots Friday to 199,469 contracts, its highest level since February this year when spot gold slid to a four year low at $336.90.

In addition, fears of further European central bank gold sales have also weighed on the market, while seasonal demand from India, the world's largest consumer, is seen tailing off during the monsoon season.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $333.70/20, compared to the London Monday afternoon fix at $334.55 an ounce.
Earlier gold had fixed Monday morning at $334.05, its lowest level since March 30, 1993. In New York Friday spot gold ended quoted around $334.3/80.
COMEX September silver ended down 7.77 cents at $4.648 an ounce, after seeing a new life-of-contract low at $4.630.
Heavy fund selling in silver, combined with the execution of stop orders below the $4.70 level in August silver, drove prices lower, traders said.
COMEX August silver had been in a $4.70-4.90 range for the past two months.
Monday is first notice for COMEX July silver and NYMEX July platinum.
NYMEX October platinum ended up $6.30 at $412.80 an ounce, but NYMEX September palladium closed off $1.30 at $174.90.

Russian officials said earlier this month that exports of PGMs would resume in late June, but that deadline looks like passing without any metal being delivered, as the original late-May deadline did, traders said.
Russia supplies about 60 pct of the world's palladium and 20 pct of its platinum and exports have been suspended since December 1996, pushing spot prices and forward rates sharply higher.
In the physical market, palladium sponge was again at a premium to ingot for Zurich delivery, with good demand from Japanese fabricators, due to the absence of Russian metal, traders said.
One month platinum lease rates were seen around 60 pct Monday, while one month palladium rates were around 80 pct.

"At around 80 per annum, fabricators are still keen to borrow metal as it costs around $12 a month only to borrow it, against say a $50 an ounce downside risk in the price when the Russian resume exports," one PGM finance house dealer said.
"My feeling is at least in U.S. there's probably enough PGMs around still to get us into July, but after that who knows," he said.
"There's been a lot of damage done here, and fabricators will be looking to use less palladium in future."

Meanwhile, an additional source of demand for PGMs is emerging in the U.S., with the U.S. Mint reporting the platinum Eagle Proof coin sets have been selling quickly since marketing began on June 6, due to the run up in platinum prices in the past few months.
((Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, 212-859-1641))
